message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$8,920 total), which is 0.13% above the $222.70 last price and well within the mandate's $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps (this was my only order today, and it was a buy of an in-mandate name, with no money moved out of the account). The case rests on Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter (ended Sept 28, 2024), reported Oct 31: quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year results confirmed in the 10-K filed Nov 1 — revenue of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08 (the latter depressed by a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge, so underlying earnings power is better than the headline). News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, which is a catalyst still in early innings rather than a fully priced-in story. I deliberately ignored a third-party "earnings recap" page whose content was quarantined by the security screen, relying instead on Apple's newsroom release and the SEC 10-K figures. Given solid growth, a strong capital-return program, and a valuation that isn't stretched relative to the franchise, I sized the position modestly (about 18% of available cash) rather than fully using the daily allowance, leaving room to add on weakness.

Order filled at 223.00, 40 shares = $8,920. Under $10k per order, total today $8,920 < $20k. Buy only, AAPL allowed, limit close to market (222.70 → 223.00, +0.13%).
